Three scenarios to show how our expertise can address business challenges.

ILLUSTRATIVE SCENARIOSThese scenarios describe possible engagements and potential deliverables. They are not client references or results of completed engagements.

01FINANCE · AUDIT & GOVERNANCE

Give leadership a clear view of IT controls.

A financial organisation wants to structure its view of IT risks and controls.

Related expertise ↗

The illustrative context

Procedures and control evidence are spread across several teams. Leadership wants to identify priority issues before defining an action plan.

The proposed approach

Define the scope with the relevant owners, examine evidence, review access and IT processes, then connect findings to business priorities.

Potential deliverables

A map of risks and controls, an executive summary and a prioritised action plan with owners and deadlines to agree.

Discuss a similar challenge ↗
02HOSPITALITY · CYBERSECURITY

Prioritise security while keeping operations in focus.

A hospitality business wants better control of exposure across endpoints, access and infrastructure.

Related expertise ↗

The illustrative context

Service continuity is essential while devices and usage patterns keep expanding. The business wants to distinguish urgent actions from changes that need planning.

The proposed approach

Review identities, configurations, backups and existing safeguards. Prioritise gaps and plan hardening measures around operational constraints.

Potential deliverables

A security baseline, configuration recommendations and a remediation roadmap tailored to the agreed scope.

Discuss a similar challenge ↗
03BUSINESS · DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION

Connect digital projects through a shared roadmap.

A growing business wants to coordinate IT investments and projects around its business priorities.

Related expertise ↗

The illustrative context

Business needs are changing and several initiatives overlap. The organisation wants to clarify its target state, dependencies and upcoming decisions.

The proposed approach

Gather needs, assess the current environment, define target-state guidelines and organise a project portfolio covering governance, security and change management.

Potential deliverables

An IT master plan, prioritisation criteria and a roadmap with milestones, dependencies and oversight arrangements.
